items.item_text: Possession of active license issued by the State of CA Board of Vocational Nurse Examiners with Intravenous Therapy and Blood Withdrawal
Possession of active BLS/CPR Certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross
Experience performing phlebotomy, injections, CPR, and other skills within scope of practice
Minimum of six months of experience working as an LVN in an outpatient ambulatory clinic or a similar healthcare setting.

Looking for a role that offers variety, flexibility, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact every day? Join UCLA Health’s Ambulatory Float Team as a Licensed Vocational Nurse, delivering patient care across diverse specialties, including Primary and Specialty Care and Cancer Care practices.

We’re seeking an adaptable, proactive professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment. You’ll collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, support clinic operations, and provide coverage across multiple practices based on staffing needs. No two days are the same, offering continuous opportunities to strengthen your clinical expertise and make a difference across UCLA Health’s ambulatory network. If you’re flexible, dependable, and passionate about patient care, we’d love to hear from you!

As a Per Diem employee on the Ambulatory Float Team, you must be available for a minimum of two weekdays per week, Monday through Friday between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., and one weekend per month, Saturday and Sunday, between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. A full month's availability must be submitted at least one month in advance.
We require completion of two consecutive weeks of full-time training, Monday through Friday, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. PST, although the schedule may vary based on training and operational needs.

Travel to UCLA Health Ambulatory Community Clinics throughout the San Luis Obispo region is required, with assigned work locations varying based on operational needs. Employees must be physically present at their assigned worksites.
Ability to be highly flexible, travel to multiple work sites within UCLA Health community based practices and work a variable schedule
Ability to take vital signs, administer medications, and obtain drug refills
Interpersonal skills in maintaining a cooperative working environment with the physicians, staff, and all health providers.
Knowledge of all instruments and supplies to perform physical examinations and procedure
